title: Right-horn and vertex-fiber comparisons for cone unstraightening
statement:
Use the small simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the projective diagram category and ordinary adjunction $L_S\dashv U_S$ of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction], and the cosimplicial pinched cubes $Q^\bullet$ and maps $Q^m\to\Delta^m$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $S$ be any small simplicial set, without a quasicategory assumption. For every $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ and $0<i\leq n$, $n\geq1$, the map
$$L_S(\Lambda_i^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\longrightarrow L_S(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)$$
is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. For any map $u:T\to S$ and any enriched presheaf $F:\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$, the simplexwise cone formula gives a natural isomorphism
$$u^*U_S(F)\cong U_T(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}}),$$
compatible with composition of base maps and natural in $F$. For a vertex $s$ of $S$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$(U_SF)_s\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q(F(s)),\qquad (\operatorname{Sing}_Q K)_m=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^m,K).$$
The simplex operators on $\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$ are precomposition with those of $Q^\bullet$. If $K$ is Kan then $\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$ is Kan and the natural map $K\to\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$ induced by $Q^m\to\Delta^m$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. These fiber comparisons are natural in maps between Kan complexes.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1; only the right-horn preservation part of the first assertion of Theorem 2.2.1.2, printed p.74; Proposition 2.2.2.9 and Remark 2.2.2.11, printed p.77. This assertion does not assume any slice model structure or the final Quillen-equivalence clause; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: Put $H=\Lambda_i^n$ and $D=\Delta^n$, with the given map $D\to S$, and write $A=S\amalg_H(H\star\Delta^0)$ and $B=S\amalg_D(D\star\Delta^0)$. In $D\star\Delta^0=\Delta^{n+1}$ the subset $P=D\cup_H(H\star\Delta^0)$ is exactly $\Lambda_i^{n+1}$: its face omitting the last vertex is $D$, and its other included faces are the cones on the faces of $D$ other than face $i$. This is an equality in every degree, since a simplex either avoids the cone vertex or is a simplex of $H$ followed by cone vertices. The universal properties of pushouts give $B=A\amalg_P\Delta^{n+1}$: a map out of either side is a map from $S$ and a map from $D\star\Delta^0$ agreeing on $D$. The inequality $0<i\leq n$ says that $P\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ is an inner horn. Thus $A\to B$ is inner anodyne, by the pushout closure in [lem-coef-coherent-inner-anodyne-equivalences], and that node makes $\mathfrak C[A]\to\mathfrak C[B]$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Apply the final preservation assertion of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] to $H\to D$ over $S$: it gives the required objectwise weak homotopy equivalence $L_S(H)\to L_S(D)$. The horn description is that of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The argument includes $n=1,i=1$, when $P$ is the two-edge inner horn in $\Delta^2$, and does not require the simplex map to be injective or $S$ to be a quasicategory.

source.place: §2.2.1, first preservation assertion in Theorem 2.2.1.2; agent expansion of the right-horn case by a single coned inner-horn pushout, using the existing coherent inner-anodyne theorem.

proof.text: Here is the simplexwise description needed for base change, directly from the pushout defining $L_S$ in [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. For a simplicial category $C$ and a presheaf $G:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$, form the category $E_G$ by adjoining one object $v$ with $E_G(c,v)=G(c)$, $E_G(v,c)=\varnothing$ and $E_G(v,v)=\Delta^0$; on the old objects it is $C$. Mixed composition is the action of $G$, so associativity and identities are precisely the presheaf axioms. A natural transformation $L_S(\Delta^m\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to F$ is equivalent to a functor $T_\sigma\to E_F$ fixing $\mathfrak C[S]$ and $v$: its old-to-$v$ maps are exactly the components of the transformation, and compatibility with composition is exactly its naturality. By the defining pushout it is therefore equivalent to a functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m\star\Delta^0]\to E_F$ whose initial-face restriction is the specified $\mathfrak C[\sigma]$ and whose cone vertex is $v$. Concretely, its mixed maps have domains $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m\star\Delta^0](j,v)$ and targets $F(\sigma(j))$; their compatibility equations use only $F$ applied to $\mathfrak C[\sigma]$ on initial-face arrows. For $\tau:\Delta^m\to T$ and $\sigma=u\tau$, these are exactly the domains, targets and equations for the presheaf $F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $\tau$, since $\mathfrak C[u\tau]=\mathfrak C[u]\mathfrak C[\tau]$. Keeping each mixed map unchanged gives inverse degreewise bijections between the two sides of the asserted base-change isomorphism. A simplex operator restricts the same cone functor on both sides. Thus these bijections are simplicial. Postcomposition by a map of presheaves and successive substitution of base maps change the same mixed maps in either order; an identity base map changes nothing. This proves naturality and compatibility with identities and composites, for arbitrary $F$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1; explicit pushout/collage calculation of the right-adjoint base-change isomorphism.

proof.text: Take the base vertex map $\{s\}\to S$ in Step 2. In the cone-functor description over its constant $m$-simplex, every initial vertex maps to $s$ and every initial-face arrow maps to $1_s$. All mixed targets are consequently $F(s)$ and all initial-face actions are identities. Thus the mixed data factor uniquely through the enriched pushout obtained by collapsing the whole initial $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ to one object $x$. To justify that this pushout is $\mathfrak C[J^m]$, use the simplex-colimit construction in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]: an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[X]\to E$ is a compatible family of functors on all simplex categories $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r]$ of $X$, hence a simplicial map $X\to N_E$, where $(N_E)_r$ is that set of enriched functors and operators are restriction. Maps out of a simplicial pushout are agreeing pairs of such maps, so $\mathfrak C$ preserves this pushout. The resulting two-object category has mixed mapping set $Q^m=\mathfrak C[J^m](x,y)$ by that cited statement; its reverse mapping set is empty and its endomorphisms are identities, as follows already from the ordered cone, since no nonidentity composable path leaves $y$ or returns to $x$. Therefore its functors to the corresponding two-object category with mixed mapping set $F(s)$ are precisely simplicial maps $Q^m\to F(s)$. This proves the fiber bijection. Restricting the initial face along $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ induces the map $Q^r\to Q^m$ specified in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], so the bijections give exactly the displayed simplicial isomorphism, with the stated operators. Postcomposing each mixed map proves naturality in $F(s)$. No Kan hypothesis was used.

source.place: §2.2.2, definition of J and Q and Remark 2.2.2.11; explicit factorization through the pinched-cone pushout.

proof.text: Write $V(X)=\int^{[m]}X_m\cdot Q^m$, where the dot is a coproduct of copies, explicitly the quotient of $\coprod_m X_m\times Q^m$ by $(X(\alpha)z,q)\sim(z,Q(\alpha)q)$. A map $V(X)\to K$ is exactly a family of maps $Q^m\to K$ indexed by $z\in X_m$, compatible with these operators. Thus $V\dashv R$, where $R(K)=\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$, by inverse assignments on those families; $V$ preserves small colimits, since compatible maps out of either colimit are the same families. Evaluation $[\alpha,q]\mapsto Q(\alpha)q$ identifies $V(\Delta^m)$ with $Q^m$, with inverse $q\mapsto[\mathrm{id}_{[m]},q]$. On $\partial\Delta^m$, every simplex factors through the proper face given by its image; the same quotient relations identify its value with the colimit over proper injective faces, namely $L_mQ$. Consequently $V(\partial\Delta^m)\to V(\Delta^m)$ is the latching monomorphism of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], including $\varnothing\to Q^0$ at $m=0$. The collapse $Q^m\to Q^0=\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by that same statement. In the Kan model category of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], apply [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] to $V$. It preserves monomorphisms as cofibrations, weak homotopy equivalences as weak homotopy equivalences, and trivial cofibrations as trivial cofibrations. In particular $V$ sends every horn inclusion to a trivial cofibration. A horn lifting problem for $R(K)\to\Delta^0$ is adjoint to lifting its image under $V$ against $K\to\Delta^0$; when $K$ is Kan, the Kan model lifting axiom supplies the filler. Hence $R(K)$ is Kan. These assertions use only the Kan model on simplicial sets, with no model structure on a slice.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.9, first assertion; coend adjunction, boundary evaluation and the existing boundary-collapse criterion expand the cofibration and right-adjoint fibrancy arguments.

proof.text: Let $p:V\to\mathrm{id}$ be induced by $p_m:Q^m\to\Delta^m$ from [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], so that $p_X([z,q])=z(p_m(q))$. This is well-defined and natural because the $p_m$ commute with every monotone map. Each $p_{\Delta^m}=p_m$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: $Q^m$ is weakly contractible by the cited node, and the realization of $\Delta^m$ is its ordinary topological simplex, which contracts by $(t,a)\mapsto(1-a)t+ae_0$. The latter realization identification sends $[\alpha,t]$ to $\alpha_*t$ and has inverse $t\mapsto[\mathrm{id},t]$, by the quotient relation in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Two-out-of-three in the Kan model of Step 4 now applies. We prove that $p_X$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $X$. It holds for $\varnothing$, since $V(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. Induct on the bound $d$ for the dimension of a simplicial set, starting with bound $-1$ for the empty set. The relative skeletal presentation of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], applied to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X$, attaches all nondegenerate $d$-simplices to the $(d-1)$-skeleton along their boundaries. After applying $V$, this remains a pushout; the coproduct of boundary maps is a monomorphism by Step 4. The three maps comparing the two attaching spans are weak homotopy equivalences: the old skeleton and the copies of $\partial\Delta^d$ by the induction hypothesis, and the copies of $Q^d\to\Delta^d$ by the simplex case. Coproducts of weak homotopy equivalences are weak homotopy equivalences directly from the realization definition: the realization quotient of a disjoint union is the disjoint union of the realizations; its path components are the disjoint unions of theirs, and a based cube or a based cube homotopy has connected domain and stays in its chosen open-and-closed summand. Apply the pushout assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to these spans. This proves the induction step, including $d=0$ with empty boundaries. For arbitrary $X$, the same skeletal presentation expresses $X$ as the colimit of its finite-dimensional skeleta indexed by the small directed poset $\mathbb N$. The colimit-preserving $V$ gives the corresponding colimit of $V$ of the skeleta. The filtered-colimit assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] applied to the natural maps $p$ proves the result for $X$. All coproducts and index sets are small in a sufficiently large fixed universe.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7 and its cellular proof; arbitrary coproduct and sequential skeletal-union details supplied explicitly, using the existing gluing/filtered-colimit lemma.

proof.text: The Quillen adjunction $V\dashv R$ from Step 4 has left derived functor naturally isomorphic to the identity: every simplicial set is cofibrant in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $V$ preserves weak homotopy equivalences, and the natural transformation $p_X$ of Step 5 has weak-equivalence components. It therefore descends to a natural isomorphism on the homotopy category, including its naturality squares. In particular the left derived functor is an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] to the Kan model category on both sides and a fibrant $K$. The ordinary counit $\epsilon_K:V R K\to K$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, since $RK$ is cofibrant (as is every simplicial set). Define $\tau_K:K\to RK$ in degree $m$ by $z\mapsto z\circ p_m$; this is the map in the item. On a coend representative $[z,q]$ the composite $\epsilon_K V(\tau_K)$ evaluates $z\circ p_m$ at $q$, so it equals $p_K$ exactly. Both $\epsilon_K$ and $p_K$ are weak homotopy equivalences, hence $V(\tau_K)$ is one. Naturality of $p$ gives the exact equation $p_{RK}V(\tau_K)=\tau_Kp_K$. The first map on the left and $p_K$ are weak homotopy equivalences by Step 5. Two-out-of-three therefore makes $\tau_K$ a weak homotopy equivalence, as required. This checks the specified natural map itself, without replacing it by an unspecified equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.9, Corollary 2.2.2.10 and Remark 2.2.2.11; derived-counit criterion and two explicit natural-transformation identities identify the required comparison map.

proof.text: For a simplicial map $h:K\to K'$, the two composites from $K$ to $RK'$ in the naturality square for $\tau$ send $z$ to $h\circ z\circ p_m$, so they agree in every degree. The fiber isomorphisms of Step 3 postcompose the same mixed maps by $h$, and consequently commute with these comparison maps. This proves the final naturality clause for all maps between Kan complexes. If $S$ or $T$ is empty there are no simplices over that base and the base-change bijections of Step 2 are the unique ones. At $m=0$, $Q^0=\Delta^0$ makes the fiber bijection and $\tau_K$ the identity on vertices. If $K=\varnothing$, every $Q^m$ is nonempty (in its explicit nonempty-subset quotient it has vertices), so $R(K)=\varnothing$; it is Kan and its empty comparison is a weak homotopy equivalence. No argument has imposed a nonemptiness, quasicategory, or projective-cofibrancy hypothesis on the inputs in the statement.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.11 and Proposition 2.2.1.1; direct naturality and degree-zero/empty-input checks of the preceding formulas.

proof_origin.place: HTT Proposition 2.2.1.1, the right-horn preservation part of Theorem 2.2.1.2, and §2.2.2 (Propositions 2.2.2.7 and 2.2.2.9, Corollary 2.2.2.10, Remark 2.2.2.11), printed pp.74–77, read online. Archival HTT WANTED. Agent-expanded coned-inner-horn, collage/base-change, pinched-fiber, coend/cellular and counit calculations, using existing nodes and no slice model structure. No Stacks tag states the specialized coherent-realization result.
